[SWS_EM_02034] Behavior after termination of all Processes managed by Exe-
cution Management
Upstream requirements:
RS_EM_00150
⌈
After all
Processes
managed by Execution Management are terminated, a post-
cleanup action shall be called.
⌋
The mechanism for invoking pre- and post-cleanup function is Platform specific. There
is no requirement on which actions should be taken at each stage.
It is not possible to give an exhaustive of list of when the
Unrecoverable State
is entered. Potential examples when the
Unrecoverable State
should be entered
include:
• The underlying OS is not functioning as expected – for example failure of
SIGKILL
(i.e.
Execution Management
cannot kill
Processes
).
•
Execution Management
has lost the ability to read the
Processed Mani-
fest
, i.e. nothing can be started / stopped.
•
Execution Management
cannot deliver responses (i.e. result of the requested
Function Group
state transitions) to
State Management
. Essentially
Exe-
cution Management
will never respond back to SM for technical reasons.
• Trusted platform configuration cannot be read meaning
Execution Manage-
ment
does not know it should run in a
strictMode
or
monitorMode
.
Note:
Unrecoverable State
should not be entered if
Execution Management
can normally communicate with
State Management
– in this case it is
State Man-
agement
’s responsibility to handle system errors (i.e. failed startup attempts).
